6. The Question on the Limbs of the Cloud “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five limbs of the cloud are to be adopted,’ which are those five limbs that are to be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the cloud allays the dust and dirt that have arisen;”
In the same way, Great King, the dust and dirt of the defilements that have arisen must be stilled by the yogin, the practitioner of yoga.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the cloud that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the cloud extinguishes the heat of the earth.
In the same way, Great King, the world together with its devas must be quenched by the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, through the cultivation of loving-kindness (*mettā*).
This, Great King, is the second quality of the cloud that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the cloud causes all seeds to sprout.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, having generated faith in all beings, should plant that seed of faith in three kinds of excellence:
in celestial and human excellences of happiness, up to the excellence of the ultimate bliss of Nibbāna.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the cloud that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a cloud, having arisen from the heat, protects the grasses, trees, creepers, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest giants growing upon the surface of the earth.

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, having generated wise attention (*yoniso manasikāra*), must protect the duty of a recluse (*samaṇadhamma*) by means of that wise attention; for all wholesome states have their root in wise attention.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the cloud that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, just as a cloud, while raining, fills the rivers, ponds, lotus-pools, caves, gullies, lakes, pools, and wells with streams of water;
even so, Great King, should a practitioner devoted to yoga, having caused the rain-cloud of the Dhamma to fall through mastery of the scriptures, fill the minds of those who desire realization.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the cloud that should be adopted.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
“Having seen a person capable of being awakened,
even if they are a hundred thousand yojanas away;”
"Having approached in an instant,
the Great Sage awakened him. Thus ends the sixth question, on the limbs of the cloud.
